title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered and executed CAND-2026-001, a paired confirmatory experiment that tests whether inserting a selective low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM-generated network-change proposals while meeting a latency SLO. We ran 400 deterministically generated paired intents (10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants) with a single generator (declared: gpt-5-mini) and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth. Results (artifact-backed): baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000), paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Planned model-call accounting enumerated 800 generations under an independent-generation convention; the executed preregistered shared-initial design produced model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair) and is reconciled in archived manifests. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) cannot be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry was not archived for the confirmatory run; we disclose this missingness and supply full provenance for all raw outputs, scorer JSONs, validator traces, and provider-call logs (SHA‑256 cataloged in the execution manifest). We interpret the artifact-backed safety numbers, discuss ceiling effects and shared-initial estimand implications, and provide reproducible next-step recommendations.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from high-level operator intent into vendor configuration promises large operational gains but risks unsafe changes if generated proposals violate interdependent network invariants. The generate–validate–repair pattern—(1) generate candidate, (2) validate against a semantic checker / digital twin, (3) repair or escalate—has emerged as a practical guardrail. However, full verification can add latency that conflicts with operational SLAs. We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) a paired experiment that measures whether a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast verifier) inserted before committing LLM-proposed changes reduces unsafe commits relative to LLM-only while meeting a preregistered latency SLO. The study was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock; all raw outputs and per-episode artifacts are archived and SHA‑256 hashed in the execution manifest.
Research question and contributions. RQ: Does a selective low-latency verification tier reduce unsafe commits relative to LLM-only generation while meeting an end-to-end latency SLO? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, paired confirmatory run with full artifact provenance using gpt-5-mini as declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the ground truth checker; (2) a deterministic reconciliation of planned vs observed model-call accounting under a preregistered shared-initial design (observed model_calls_used = 401 vs planned_model_calls = 800 conventionally enumerated); (3) artifact-grounded primary results and their statistical treatment; (4) disclosure of missing latency telemetry and concrete reproducible recommendations.
sections.related_work: We situate this work among recent efforts on LLM-driven NetOps, generate–validate–repair pipelines, and verifier-augmented agentic systems. Representative artifact-backed nearest work includes Cornetto-style configuration-repair benchmarks and evaluations of verifier-augmented agents (archived items: arXiv:2604.22513; arXiv:2606.06212; arXiv:2604.18233). Formal verification and digital-twin validation research provide the semantic-checker foundations used here (e.g., NetKAT/SMT-based and header-space analyses; see cited bibliographic items archived in the evidence bundle). Prior works stress that LLM proposals frequently introduce regressions and argue for verifier-guided iterative workflows; our experiment tests a latency-aware selective verification intervention under a rigorously preregistered design and full artifact archiving.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes; the preregistration (study plan, hypotheses H1/H2, estimands, sampling, retry/missingness rules, analysis scripts) is archived and immutable (see execution manifest). Primary confirmatory hypotheses: H1 (safety) — selective verification yields a lower unsafe-commit rate than LLM-only (paired comparison); H2 (latency) — 95th-percentile end-to-end latency ≤ 2000 ms and materially lower than a full-verification baseline. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline.
Corpus and tasks. A deterministic synthetic task generator created 400 paired intents (CNSM-SelectiveVerify-SyntheticCorpus-v1); 40/400 (10%) are preregistered adversarial/OOD variants via deterministic perturbation rules. Tasks model operationally meaningful changes (interface MTU/VLAN edits, uplink failovers, rolling migrations) and embed dependency constraints (must-down-before-MTU, make-before-break for uplinks, minimum-active-in-group). Example task mapping: pair-000001 (task manifest and full responses archived at execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 ea8359dbe5a5...). The task manifests include initial and expected final states, explicit required sequences, and safety constraints.
Intervention and baseline. Baseline = LLM-only candidate accepted for final scoring. Guarded = risk-scoring + fast verifier applied to the same shared-initial candidate (preregistered shared-initial design) and, if flagged, an automated fast repair step before final deterministic scoring. The deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) computed the binary outcome (valid/unsafe) per episode and produced detailed validator traces archived per episode (execution/scoring/*.json).
Shared-initial candidate design and model-call accounting. To reduce generator variance and isolate verifier/repair effects the preregistration permitted a shared-initial candidate per intent (independent_condition_generation=false). Under the independent-generation accounting convention the preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 (400 intents × 2 conditions × 1 generation). Executed model-call accounting followed the shared-initial protocol and produced model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair). We preregistered this possibility and reconciled the counts deterministically; the execution manifest and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json document the provider-call audit (stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation":400, "repair":1}) and list all provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/). This reconciliation is artifact-backable and included in the Disclosure Statement.
Scoring and analysis. Per-episode verifier verdicts (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were stored as JSONs (execution/scoring/...). The primary test used exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI was computed with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). Missingness and retry policies were followed: no unrecovered infrastructure failures occurred; complete_pair_count = 400. All analysis scripts and result artifacts are archived (analysis/).
sections.results:
Confirmatory results (artifact-backed). Complete pairs: 400. Baseline valid proposals: 399/400 (0.9975). Guarded valid proposals: 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 a6906bb4...). Primary estimand (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Analysis artifacts: condition_summary.csv and paired_contingency_table.csv (archived; SHA‑256s recorded). Representative per-episode scorer/validator JSONs and shared-initial responses are archived (examples below).
Representative artifact-grounded example (discordant episode). The sole discordant pair (n10 = 1; guarded valid, baseline invalid) is available for inspection: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (baseline scorer: SHA‑256 fe147f43...), execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (guarded scorer: SHA‑256 d0cbfe9a...), and the shared-initial candidate and provider-call trace for that pair are archived. The per-episode validator traces show the baseline candidate failed a dependency check; the guarded pipeline corrected/avoided it and thus scored valid. Exact paths and SHA‑256s are in the execution manifest and in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation. The observed absolute safety gain is small (0.25 percentage points) because baseline generation performance (with this generator, this synthetic corpus, and the deterministic validator) was already very high. A near-ceiling baseline constrains observable gains and reduces power to detect small but operationally meaningful improvements. The paired exact p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0075] quantify that uncertainty. Practitioners should read our result as — in this controlled setting with a near-perfect generator/validator pairing and shared-initial candidates, selective fast verification produced a numerically tiny improvement; larger safety gains are likely in settings with weaker generators, different validators, or broader adversarial exposure.
Shared-initial estimand: operational meaning and trade-offs. The preregistered shared-initial candidate protocol intentionally conditions on identical generator outputs across conditions, isolating verifier/repair effects per candidate. That estimand answers: given the same generated candidate, does selective verification + repair improve acceptance safety? It does not measure the joint effect when the generator is independently re-sampled per condition: independent_generation would measure end-to-end pipeline differences including generator variability. Both estimands are useful; we document the design choice, reconcile the model-call accounting (planned versus executed), and archive provider-call logs so readers can reproduce either estimand in future runs. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) show model_calls_used=401 and provider-call stage_counts.
Missing preregistered telemetry and consequences for H2. The preregistered H2 required artifact-backed end-to-end latency telemetry (95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms). The confirmatory run did not archive per-stage timing traces; consequently H2 is unresolved from these artifacts. We explicitly disclose this missingness in the execution log and analysis artifacts rather than impute or invent latency numbers. Future artifact-grounded repeats must record per-stage timestamps (generation, risk-scoring, fast-verifier, full-checker) to test latency hypotheses and compute 95th-percentiles with bootstrap CIs.
Failure analysis and diagnostic utility. The single discordant example provides a compact failure-mode diagnostic: baseline candidate violated a dependency (validator-detected) while the guarded pipeline repaired/avoided it. The full per-episode JSONs, shared-initial candidate, and provider-call trace permit reproducible replay and deeper root-cause analysis. We encourage researchers to inspect archived per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) to classify concrete failure modes and guide targeted mitigations such as adversarial detection or model fine-tuning.
Threats to validity. Internal: shared-initial design affects estimand; single generator (gpt-5-mini) and deterministic validator reduce generality; deterministic synthetic corpus may not capture natural operator phrasing. Construct: the deterministic validator approximates functional correctness but may diverge from real-device behavior; our digital-twin semantics are archived for inspection. External: single-model and single-validator scope, synthetic tasks, and absence of real production heterogeneity limit broad generalization. Conclusion validity: near-ceiling baseline constrains effect size detectability and practical interpretation. All threats are discussed and recorded in the Limitations section and in archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, provenance-rich paired experiment to assess a latency-aware selective verification intervention in LLM-driven NetOps pipelines. Artifact-backed results show a very small absolute safety improvement (0.25 percentage points) against a near-ceiling baseline; statistical evidence is inconclusive for a nonzero effect in this setting. The run exposed crucial operational and design issues: (1) shared-initial vs independent-generation estimand differences and their model-call accounting consequences (observed model_calls_used = 401 vs planned 800 under a different accounting convention), (2) the requirement to archive per-stage latency telemetry to evaluate latency SLOs (H2 unresolved here), and (3) the reproducible value of per-episode validator traces for failure-mode analysis. All raw outputs, per-episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (execution manifest). We recommend follow-up artifact-backed runs that (a) record per-stage timing, (b) sweep selective-verifier thresholds over larger adversarial proportions to map a verification-budget vs unsafe-commit Pareto frontier, and (c) test multiple generator/validator families to improve external validity. The entire confirmatory run, artifacts, and deterministic reconciliation are available in the archived execution bundle (paths and SHA‑256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest).

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory, artifact-backed):
- Initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial constraints before the autonomy lock. All study formulation, frozen preregistration (CAND-2026-001), experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI-based peer review, and revision were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock; no human edited technical manuscript content post-lock.
- Model and orchestration: declared generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived; SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab...), adapter/orchestration family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The run used the preregistered shared-initial candidate protocol (independent_condition_generation=false) as allowed by the preregistration.
- Preregistration: CAND-2026-001 preregistration artifact (study plan, hypotheses H1/H2, sampling plan, retry/missingness rules, analysis scripts) was frozen before observing outcomes and is archived (preregistration SHA‑256: 086d248e8963...). Primary analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Power, sampling, and exclusion rules are recorded in the preregistration.
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the functional ground-truth checker and per-episode scorer (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). All per-episode scorer JSONs reside at execution/scoring/*.json and are SHA‑256 hashed in the execution manifest.
- Execution provenance and artifacts: All raw model responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), validator traces, provider-call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), execution log (execution/execution_log.jsonl), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), and analysis artifacts (analysis/...) are archived with SHA‑256 values in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Representative artifact examples referenced in this manuscript include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: ea8359dbe5a5...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: 431f61c02fac...), and the single discordant pair artifacts execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...).
- Model-call accounting and reconciliation: the preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 under an independent-generation convention. The executed shared-initial design produced model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared-initial + 1 repair); this deterministic reconciliation and the provider-call audit (stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":400, "repair":1}) are archived in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest.
- Missing preregistered telemetry: the preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th-percentile ≤ 2000 ms) required archived per-stage end-to-end timing telemetry. Those per-stage timing traces were not recorded in the confirmatory artifact bundle; H2 is therefore unresolved from the archived run. This absence is logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis logs; no latency claims are made without archived telemetry.
- Human involvement: pre-lock humans set topic constraints and developed execution infrastructure; all post-lock research steps (literature synthesis, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript generation, AI peer-review, and revision) were autonomous. No manual technical edits were made to manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
- Reproducibility: every reported number and per-episode decision is reproducible from the archived artifacts and SHA‑256 manifest. Analysts with the artifact bundle can replay provider-call logs and validator traces to reproduce the analysis. The full execution manifest lists all archived files and their hashes.
limitations: Synthetic confirmatory corpus: deterministic generator tasks may not capture natural operator language diversity or production heterogeneity.
Single-model scope: experiments declared gpt-5-mini only; results do not generalize across LLM families without additional runs.
Single deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a digital-twin approximation and may not perfectly match real-device behavior.

Shared-initial design affects estimand: the chosen design conditions on identical generator outputs per intent and isolates verifier/repair effects; it differs from an independent-generation estimand that re-samples the generator per condition.
Latency SLO unresolved: preregistered H2 required per-stage latency telemetry which was not archived; therefore latency claims cannot be made from these artifacts.
